title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The right side is a sorted list of runs of 1s of lengths 13 + 6i, separated by 00, with fewer runs of each larger length: a counter in some mixed base, measured, not proved. The machine runs step for step like 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- (another batch) on the tape. Halting needs F on a 1, entered only from E on a 1; never one step away in the first 3·106 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,151 cells have been visited and 22,314 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.162).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rules: D crosses (01)^n rightward turning it into (11)^n (2 steps per copy), and C crosses a run of 1s leftward (1 step per cell).

claims.title: A sorted list of runs 1^(13+6i)
claims.text: At the last right extension before 109 steps (step 948,962,681) the right part of the tape is 1,008 runs of 1s separated by 00: 616 runs 1^13, then 188 of 1^19, 121 of 1^25, 37 of 1^31, 22 of 1^37, 7 of 1^43, 4 of 1^49, and single runs 1^53, 1^59, 1^63, with a few short runs (7, 13, 17, 21, 27, 35, 40, 47) in between, which are the places being worked on. Left of it: (100)^3061 1^5 (001111111)^932 1100, the bouncer's region.

claims.title: Same tape as a machine in another batch
claims.text: 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- has the same triage numbers; sampled every 99,991 steps to 2·10<sup>6</sup>, and at 2·10<sup>8</sup>, the two machines have the same tape and number of 1s except at moments when the head is in the part where their tables differ (D1, E0).

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1 (E1 → 0RF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps E reads a 1 374,145 times, always with a 0 to its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of runs behaves like a counter (each length 13 + 6i a digit, its multiplicity the digit's value, carries making longer runs), but the carry rule is not written down, let alone proved.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tape and head as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- at every one of the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the tables differ). The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_1LD0RF_0RA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RE_1LA1LC_1RB0LF_0LC--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

python3 holdouts/1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD---/py/observe.py 1e7 B 6      # the tape at the last moments each end grew

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps, on the right of its tape, a sorted list of runs of 1s whose lengths go up in steps of 6, fewer of each length than of the one before. This page shows that list and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,151 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A sorted list of runs of 1s
html: At step 948,962,681 the right part of the tape is 1,008 runs of 1s separated by 0 0:

(1^13 is thirteen 1s.) The lengths go up by 6, the runs are sorted, and there are fewer of each length than of the one before. A handful of odd short runs mark places being worked on. On the left, (100)^3061 1^5 (001111111)^932 is the bouncer's region.

sections.heading: A counter made of runs
html: Read each length 13 + 6i as a digit place and its number of runs as the digit. As the machine runs, runs grow from one length to the next and new longer runs appear at the right end (longest 59 at step 7.6·108, 63 at 9.5·108), like carries. The carry rule is not yet written down: these are measurements.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1 (moving right). In the first 3·106 steps E reads a 1 374,145 times and the next cell is always 0. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.162).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,151 cells (26,993 left of the start, 395 right), with a density of 1s of 0.601.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same run as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- (observed, not proved). At every one of the first 107 steps from blank tape the two machines have the same tape and the head on the same cell. Their tables differ, and no renaming of the states turns one into the other. While they run, the states pair up as A–A, B–B, C–C, D–D, E–B, E–E, F–E, F–F (this machine first), which is not one to one. Transitions not used in these steps: this machine never uses F1 and the other never uses F1. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean in the other machine's folder, lock_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that the two runs have the same tape, the same head position and paired states up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_1LD0RF_0RA---: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state D
  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RE_1LA1LC_1RB0LF_0LC---: rename A→D, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 8,004,076 here and step 10,000,000 there

family: bouncer feeding a sorted list of runs 1^(13+6i)
summary: A bouncer on the left; on the right a list of runs of 1s separated by 00 whose lengths are 13, 19, 25, 31, ... (13 + 6i), sorted, with multiplicities that fall off from one length to the next (616, 188, 121, 37, 22, 7, 4, 1 at 10^9 steps).
